title: Ops–Seller Sprint Choreography & Handoff (draft)
content:
Purpose

Quick working draft: a 1–2 slide per-stage choreography and short battlecard snippets for seller->ops handoffs during fast pilots. Goal: reduce ambiguity on who runs benchmarks, who validates latency/SLOs, and what fallback messages sellers use in the first 72 hours.

Audience
- Field sellers (SEs), sales ops, pilot engineers, customer success.
- Fast pilots where Dedicated/Private choices are still open.

Guiding principles (short)
- Keep scripts < 1 minute for seller openers.
- Ops owns the technical checklist; seller owns customer expectation script.
- Fail fast: if perf drift > 20% in first 24h, trigger fallback + SE play.

1) Pre-demo warmup (slide idea: 1 slide)
- Who: SE + Solutions engineer
- Timebox: 30–60 minutes before demo or pilot kickoff
- Checklist:
  - Confirm API key + routing policy to use (hosted / dedicated alias)
  - Share a short prompt-set (3 representative traces) with ops (attachment sample below)
  - Verify telemetry flags: token-level tracing ON for test client
  - Agree on success metrics (p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, quality seed tests)

Seller script (30s):
- "We'll run three quick requests that reflect how your users talk; we'll measure latency and outputs and then tune routing or model variant if needed."

2) Pilot initiation (slide: flow diagram)
- Who: SE (owner), Ops (technical runbook), CS (stakeholder comms)
- Timebox: first 4 hours after pilot start
- Ops quick tasks:
  - Confirm model version pinned and fallback model configured
  - Start prefix cache warmup (list of seed prefixes provided by SE)
  - Validate batch sizing and autoscaling window for expected QPS
  - Run smoke load: 50 requests over 5 minutes across expected seq lengths
- Seller quick checks:
  - Run 3 user-simulated prompts and capture outputs
  - Flag any hallucinations / safety hits to CS immediately

3) Contingency choreography (one slide: decision tree)
- Trigger conditions and immediate seller language:
  - Condition A: p95 latency > agreed SLO by 30% for 30m -> Seller: "We're seeing a temporary slowdown; we're going to route to an alternate model to keep UI snappy, you might see slightly different phrasing but same intent."
  - Condition B: Error rate spike (>3% 5m window) -> Ops: scale up dedicated pool + enable fallback routing; Seller: "We're applying a quick resilience change; please retry in ~60s."
  - Condition C: Quality regression (manual triage) -> Pause rollouts, notify stakeholders, open an evaluation ticket

Short fallback message templates (for sellers)
- Soft fallback (user-facing): "We're experiencing a short performance hiccup. Please retry in a few moments — your data and privacy are unaffected."
- Partial functionality: "We're switching to a faster variant for this view. Reply may be briefer but will be faster."

4) Ops runbook checklist (for pilot engineers)
- Preflight: model pin, kv cache pop, autoscale hook test, KMS access validated
- Day0 (0–4h): smoke load, trace capture, perf dashboard share link to SE
- Day1 (24h): analyze token distribution skew, update batch window, recommend quantization profile if cost > expected
- Day2 (48–72h): final go/no-go recommendation for conversion to Reserved/Dedicated

Metrics quick-reference (one-pager style)
- Comms-friendly metrics to call out to buyer:
  - p50 / p95 latency (in ms) by sequence length buckets
  - Cost per 1k tokens approximated for observed mix
  - Errors per 1k requests
  - Model quality pass rate on seed prompt set (simple binary pass/fail)

Slide-by-slide outline (6 slides total recommended)
1. One-line value prop + pilot scope (seller opener)
2. Quick architecture diagram (routing, model variants, fallback lanes)
3. Choreography timeline (Pre-demo -> Day0 -> Day1 -> Day3)
4. Playbook snippets (seller scripts and fallback messages)
5. Ops checklist & immediate run commands (copyable)
6. Decision criteria to recommend Dedicated / Private (convert)

Mini-battlecard (front pocket) — tearout bullets sellers keep in Slack
- If p95 spikes: tell customer we’ll route to faster variant; open RT ticket JIRA-RT-724; ping #pilot-ops
- If quality problem: revert to previous model version; add observed prompt to "quality-issues" confluence page
- If cost unexpectedly high: enable token sampling for non-critical responses; ops to recommend quantization profile

Open questions (notes-to-self)
- How much authority do sellers have to toggle fallback routes in Dedicated trials? Need legal/contract clarity. (Owner: Jordan)
- Should we provide a small CLI wrapper for sellers to run the 3-seed smoke tests locally? (PR exists; link above)
- Is there a short consent blurb for customers if we switch to Private / on-prem mid-pilot? Ops & Legal to weigh in.

Attachments / quick paste blocks (for SEs)
- Sample prompt-set (3 items):
  1) "Summarize recent chat thread for billing correction, keep 3 bullets"
  2) "Generate product support reply recommending next steps, empathetic tone, <= 120 tokens"
  3) "Extract invoice amount and due date from this note"

- Quick ops commands (example):
  - curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"input": "<seed prompt>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --trace=1
  - ./pilot-cli warmup --prefix-file prefixes.txt --concurrency 4

Next steps / TODOs
- Convert this draft into a 3-slide seller pack + 1-page ops checklist by 2025-11-25 (Owner: Priya)
- Validate fallback wording with legal and CS by 2025-11-27 (Owner: Marta)
- Ship pilot-CLI PR and attach stable binary to deck (Owner: Noah)

Notes: keep this intentionally terse. This is a working file for the next two sprint cycles — expect lots of small edits.

History of edits
- 2025-11-02 initial skeleton
- 2025-11-12 added contingency decision tree and commands
- 2025-11-20 tightened seller scripts and added sample prompt-set
